A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same adaptive self-improvement system for STeP library development. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated code examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on 26 STeP programming tasks, including model comparisons, self-improvement learning curves, and agent-component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds token-matched comparisons, supervised fine-tuning results, code-quality analyses, an expert pilot comparison, and an AIME-2024 evaluation.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, experience filtering and stratification, proposer/guardian agents, structural IR, and verifiers retain the same procedures. Fine-tuning is an added comparator; the generalization discussion and AIME application do not document changes to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The original 26-task STeP benchmark is retained. Appendix A.5 adds evaluation on 30 AIME-2024 mathematics problems, extending actual task coverage substantially beyond ML-library code generation.

E2.justification: Appendix A.4 introduces GPT-4o supervised fine-tuning as an evaluated alternative, using three training-data formulations summarized in Table 6, and adds a pilot domain-expert comparison. Original LLM comparators remain; Single-WS becoming Single-w/o-IR is only a rename.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce token-count matching through resampling with shared verifier access, SFT datasets containing 133/133/17 examples with evaluation on unfinished tasks, and maintainability/complexity measurements with top-per-task maintainability selection. The original sampling settings in Appendix A.3 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained difficulty, granularity, IR, and guardian analyses, v2 adds a control for token-budget and verifier-access differences, generated-code maintainability and complexity analyses, and an exploratory human-effort comparison. These address substantial additional questions about attribution and practical usefulness.

E5.justification: The original seed disclosure remains, and v2 adds no independent-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new code-property means, minima, and maxima are descriptive results rather than performance-uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original result tables and learning curves retain their values. New Table 5 reports final agent/self-improved versus single-model Pass@n of 0.96 versus 0.77 for Claude Sonnet and 0.81 versus 0.38 for GPT-4o; Table 6 reports SFT at 0.62 versus self-improvement at 0.81. AIME results increase from 0.50 to 0.67, and timing and code-quality findings are added.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 newly defines the comment-weight quantity MIcw = MI - MIwoc and states its range as [0, 49). This is a limited quantitative definition; the existing algorithmic mathematics, pass@k equation, and STeP equations remain unchanged, with no new proof or theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same algorithm, system, and benchmark contributions, including the headline 3.9× improvement and 96% task-completion claims. The conclusion adds a broader future-application outlook without revising these central claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.5 substantially expands applicability reasoning: transfer requires suitable formats, verifiers, and language-specific handling of global constraints, while familiar-language patterns may restrict exploration. Section 3.3 expands context-capacity discussion; A.4 adds interpretations of code quality and practical efficiency, acknowledges unmatched SFT FLOPs, and identifies the need for fuller human studies.

D1.justification: v2 adds SFT corpus-construction details, prompt variants, AST deduplication, use of OpenAI fine-tuning, and an AIME dataset-access reference. Existing model identifiers, temperatures, output limits, code examples, and code-access information remain; important settings for the added experiments are still unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Tree of Thoughts, AFlow, and structured MLIR code generation. Appendix A.6 also contrasts the approach with Spiral, Ansor, and AKG, modestly expanding positioning against conventional code-generation systems without evaluating them as baselines.

P1.justification: The abstract and several explanatory paragraphs receive local rewrites, some headings and terminology change, and acknowledgements and a generalization subsection are added. The main narrative order and most existing appendix explanations and code examples are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds three compact tables for token matching, fine-tuning, and code complexity; the former abbreviation Table 5 becomes Table 8. Figure 4 labels/caption and the Figure 9 legend are revised, with local repositioning and reflow rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Table 5 addresses a fairness gap in v1 by comparing methods with matched token counts and verifier access, strengthening support for the reported gains. Fine-tuning and code-quality analyses add useful validation. However, missing AIME settings, unclear reporting across the three SFT variants, and the limited human pilot constrain the evidential gains, making the overall improvement modest.
